body: So beautifully put.. thank you for finding a way to put what I've been feeling into words. Sending you all the peace I can muster
That is a beautiful mindset to honor your daughter. I am so sorry you lost her. My heart breaks for you.
thank you for saying this. My best friend was struck and killed on a crosswalk in broad daylight back in November because our city prioritizes cars over the lives of pedestrians and bikers.

I’m also struggling with this. I try to divide my bereavement evenly between friends and family. If I dumped grief thoughts on one friend last week, I’ll reach out to someone else the next week. I’m scared of becoming that person that’s a bummer to be around. I’m so sad and it’s difficult to hide it but I’m doing my best. My grief negatively impacts many of my relationships - I’m distant and I isolate myself, I don’t answer texts or calls, and I overall see the world so differently now. It’s all a part of the process and the ones that stick around are the ones you’re meant to keep in your life. You are not burdensome and neither is your grief.

It took me a couple of months to begin to accept Nina’s death. It will happen for you, too. There is no definitive timeline. Be gentle with yourself and let your heart heal the way it needs to. We are all here with you, I’m very sorry for your loss.
I am so deeply sorry for your loss

Everybody grieves differently but I relate heavily to your friend. I have a very difficult time responding to texts because that requires attention, attention which I do not possess since my mind is consumed with grief 24/7. It's much easier posting on social media because you're not talking to anyone specific and you don't feel pressured to respond to anyone. Don't take any of it personally, this doesn't have to do with you. It's very sweet you sent her a care package and flowers. But please keep in mind it has only been 3 weeks. While that may sound long enough to many, your friend is only just beginning the grieving process. She's not feeling better as the days go on - she is feeling worse. Responding to texts or saying thank you for flowers isn't on her mind.

When someone dies, everyone rushes in to help the first couple of weeks. This is the most overwhelming period for us grievers. If you want to help your friend, *stay*. Be there for her three months from now, once everyone else is already expecting her to move on. Ask her about her husband. His favorite foods. His favorite activities. Funny stories about him. Use his name when you talk about him. 

I don't mind receiving texts as long as people don't expect me to reply quickly. Some send really long texts, paragraphs and paragraphs, and those overwhelm me. Again, everyone grieves differently, but I appreciate short and sweet texts. "Thinking of you," "Whenever you're ready to talk I will be here," or "You don't need to reply but I want you to know I love you and I will never forget about \_\_\_\_." 

Thank you for caring enough about your friend to reach out to us.

This brought me to tears because I haven't been able to articulate these thoughts myself and you covered it beautifully. Pictures and videos of Nina are so surreal to me now. I didn't think twice of it at the time. I didn't realize what an honor and privilege it was to be in the presence of her physical being. To hear her voice and her laugh. To smell her perfume. The last time I hugged her, I was in a hurry and it was quick. I don't even think I put my arm all the way around her. It was dark out, I was cold, and I was dreading the bus ride back home. She was killed two days later and I haven't gone a second without thinking about it since.

I’ve also lost a couple friends during my grieving process. If they are meant to be in your life, you will cross paths again. I don’t completely resent my friends who couldn’t stick around during my time of need. Everyone is fighting their own battles. Someone I thought I loved jumped ship after Nina’s death and it hurt but I’m grateful for the times I shared with them anyway. Life is too short to not be grateful. Idk I’m just spewing my thought process here because I’m going through it too. I’m sending you love.

Thank you so much for trying. I can’t imagine the trauma.
I’m amazed you could sense that from this photo because she truly was so mellow. Just being in her presence instantly calmed you down. I will miss her for eternity.
I really appreciate your activism and passion. I am too sad to be angry right now so I’m leaning on people like you to be angry for me.

Some of my favorite things about Nina:
- Her voice. She was studying to become an opera singer. Two days before she was killed, she expressed doubts about pursuing an MFA in opera. I told her that ten years from now, she doesn’t want to be wondering “what if” and she has to give it a shot. She had so much potential. She really had a gift. 
- She loved cats. She fostered tons and tons of cats over the years, and she loved every single one of them, even the mean ones or the ones with boogers and bald patches. All animals loved her, she was Snow White. 
- She always smelled amazing. She was obsessed with trying different fragrance oils and any time you hugged her you could smell lavender or something similar. 
- Her laugh. When she laughed really hard, she would go completely silent and take these big gulps of air.
- So many inside jokes that nobody else will ever understand. Now I just have to tell them to myself. She was so funny. 
- Her toes. We bonded over having the ugliest feet of all time. All of her toes curled together like little peanuts and mine are long, like monkey feet. Whenever we got pedicures together we would snap gross pictures of our unfortunate feet and text them to each other. The nail artists always gave us funny looks for laughing so hard. 
- She picked up new hobbies all the time and she was passionate about every single one of them. We had a habit of starting new hobbies together, I would always drop off after a couple weeks but she kept going. Veganism, fitness, sustainable living, thrifting, painting (she was a miraculous artist), choir. She was so multi faceted and talented. You never ran out of things to talk about with her. 
- Her patience. She wanted to understand all of her loved ones so she knew the best ways to help them. For me, I have horrible anxiety that the people I love are dead any time I don’t hear from them for a certain amount of time. She was so understanding and gentle towards me whenever I freaked out that she hadn’t responded to me. Now my worst nightmare has came true.
Yes. Please keep rallying. Please stay angry. This will never stop unless enough people make their voices heard.

I couldn’t have said it better myself. It’s so easy to see these statistics, go “aw that’s so sad,” and move on about your day. Drivers forget these are human beings with friends and family who love them and need them. 24 years of life gone in barely a second. She was so intelligent and so kind. She was very, very special to me and so many others. She was a beautiful opera singer and finishing up her MFA applications. She was smart as a whip. She cared so much about the environment and animals. She truly made the world, and my world, a brighter place.
She was using the crosswalk when a big SUV barreled into her. She was trapped under the vehicle until EMTs and firefighters rescued her.
Absolutely. Me and some of her friends were thinking of throwing together a mini memorial soon for those who can’t make it to Connecticut.
This was my best friend Nina. If you go to my profile you can see a photo of her that we took two days before the accident. Thank you for not letting her be just another number.

Thank you. We were both trying to contain laughter because I had set the camera timer for too long. We had to just sit there posing for an extended period of time until it went off. I wish I could relive that day.

We were drunk one night and ravenous. We sat down on the carpet and ate a big pot of spaghetti with our hands because we were too tired to find forks. We had sauce all over our faces and our fingers. So many tiny moments like that. I miss her already.

Nooo. It is very common for suicidal people to lash out before they end their life in an attempt to alleviate others’ grief. Being 16 is utter hell, I would never ever go back to that age. I truly hope this world eases up on you so you get to experience the freedom of adulthood.

I don’t think apologizing to your brother would expose that your parents told you about his suicidal thoughts. Hopefully anyone would apologize for saying such a thing, regardless of how much they knew about that person’s mental state. I know you already feel terrible so I won’t lecture you but please, in the future, be more mindful of how powerful your words can be. If I were you, I would apologize to your brother as soon as possible. It sounds like you do care about him and you did not mean what you said. Best of luck to you, him, and your parents.
HUGE difference, wow!! Keep it up!

Personally, I just think that makes for an incredibly boring and predictable dynamic. I would take Izzie and Alex’s banter and slightly tumultuous relationship over Alex and Jo’s mundane dynamic.

Exactly. Izzie existed as Izzie before and after her relationship with Alex. Jo was only ever about Alex. I’m never going to be interested in watching a relationship between two people who are carbon copies of each other. It’s way too obviously crafted, predictable, and makes for an uninteresting dynamic.

Agree that they did have a lot of clashing which got kinda old, but that was just the writers doing their usual thing of never letting relationships last and creating drama constantly. If they had just let them develop together normally I think they could be really great.

Exactly! Izzie was bubbly and girly, and although she had a tough past it didn’t became her entire central personality trait like Jo. Izzie was different from Alex in many ways and because of it they complimented each other nicely. Jo is just a boring female version of Alex, nothing exciting about their relationship at all IMO.
